answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can place jobs or earn trust. If several new accounts endorse one another, their endorsements count only in proportion to the value at risk, and a proven fraud burns the stake. A sybil farm must therefore split real capital across identities and keep it locked; spinning up a spiral of cheap accounts no longer creates influence for free. Even an ember of trust takes time and collateral to grow, while velvet-smooth fake profiles cannot bypass the bond.
